### 1 — Scene
A mixed meal of bone-in roasted meats, a fresh rice-paper roll, and baby carrots.

### 2 — Vessel
A dinner plate, approximately **26 cm across**.  
Area = 3.14 × 13² ≈ **531 cm²**.

### 3 — Items
- A small bone-in shank, likely lamb
- Roasted chicken leg portion, skin-on
- Fresh rice-paper roll with noodles, lettuce, and possibly shrimp
- Four baby carrots

No separate sauce or measurable pool of oil is visible.

### 4–6 — Area, volume, and weight
Heights below represent average thickness over each item's footprint. Density is the only volume-to-weight reduction.

| Item | Plate area | Area (cm²) | Height (cm) | Gross volume (ml) | Density (g/ml) | Weight (g) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Bone-in shank | 11% | 58 | 2.8 | 162 | 0.95 | 154 |
| Chicken portion | 10% | 53 | 2.8 | 148 | 0.95 | 141 |
| Rice-paper roll | 18% | 96 | 2.4 | 230 | 0.90 | 207 |
| Baby carrots | 6% | 32 | 2.3 | 74 | 0.65 | 48 |
| **Total** | **45%** | **239** | | | | **550** |

The estimated 45% coverage is consistent with the visible gaps and broad exposed rim.

### 7 — Energy
The meat weights **include bones**. Their energy densities are therefore adjusted to the whole bone-in portion, rather than treating bone weight as edible meat.

| Item | kcal/100 g as plated | Estimated kcal |
|---|---:|---:|
| Bone-in shank | 160 | 246 |
| Bone-in roasted chicken | 175 | 247 |
| Fresh rice-paper roll | 110 | 228 |
| Baby carrots | 41 | 20 |
| **Total** | | **741** |

### 8 — Sanity check
Approximately **550 g including bones and 740 kcal** is plausible for two modest bone-in meat portions, one large fresh roll, and four carrots. The meat identification, bone content, and roll filling are the largest uncertainties.
